claims.title: Local Boolean cancellation can destroy separability without obstructing global positive partitions

status: source_derived_unreviewed; Source-reported mathematical arguments only. Intake checked byte preservation and repository structure; no independent proof reconstruction, scientific-code replay, citation verification, formal proof, quantum circuit execution, or experimental validation was performed. External correctness and historical priority remain UNKNOWN.
interface: For a finite Boolean matrix M, r(M) is real rank, pi(M) the number of disjoint positive one-rectangles, and signed length s counts Cartesian rectangles with +/-1 coefficients. The general target pi(M)<=exp(polylog(s+2)) is an existing log-rank reformulation, still OPEN. The source constructs counterexamples to specific local cancellation rules, not to log-rank, arbitrary positive partitions or communication efficiency.
limits: Audit the exact kernel factorization and imported robust-rank theorem. Seek a global cancellation/predicate operation with amortized control proving pi(M)<=exp(polylog(s+2)) from arbitrary signed length s, or precisely refute a proposed operation. Local failures do not settle this log-rank-equivalent target.
